summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 9 New Features Demonstration ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Sherry from Marvelous Designer. Today, I will introduce some new features of Marvelous Designer. ## GPU Module The first new feature is the GPU module. Wait for a project file. Here you can see two identical panels. When you click on the panel, you can see that the particle diameter of the panel is relatively small, and the size of the panel is also relatively large. Let's use a normal model to simulate the panel. You can see that the simulation speed is relatively slow. When the panel is relatively large and the particle diameter is relatively small, the computer operation speed will slow down. In the menu bar, you can select different simulation settings. There are four simulation properties. In the new version, we added GPU simulation settings. This utilizes the GPU of the computer to simulate, improving our operation speed by relying on the graphics card configuration. The second is the most commonly used normal simulation setting. This simulation is used to create costume animations. The simulation speed is relatively high; however, the computer operation speed will still slow down. The last one is the highest level simulation setting, which can restore the most authentic use of the fabric, but the simulation speed is the slowest. I do not recommend everyone to use it. If you use the GPU simulation setting, you will find that the operation speed has been significantly increased after a brief startup time. At this time, the drag surface will be very smooth, and the response speed is very fast. However, the results of GPU and CPU simulation differ. The CPU simulation is more stable, and the simulation effect is closer to the real surface, making it suitable for creating multi-layer clothing. The GPU simulation speed is faster but less stable, so if you want to make multi-layer clothing, you need to pay attention to increasing the thickness. ## Symmetry Feature In the new version, we can directly rely on the symmetry of the real version. Select a line and choose the symmetry option in the menu bar on the right. The panel will be left and right symmetrical based on the selected line. When you click on a point, the other side will also change. When we create an internal shape, the corresponding internal shape will also be created on the other side. Adjusting the internal shape position will operate simultaneously on both sides. All this can be determined by a double-click. Now, let's create a set of symmetrical versions. After creating a body prefix in the two types of overlays, the body prefix will automatically be symmetrical. If you need to cancel the symmetry relationship, you can select the middle version and click on the drop-down menu in the right-hand corner to remove the link. If you adjust the version now, the other side will not be modified simultaneously. We have set the symmetry relationship for some previous files, which can be merged to create a fully symmetrical editable version. You can see that the merge section of the version has become a virtual line. Additionally, we can also directly merge the linked version. After merging the version, click the right button to set the production effect in the menu bar. After opening, the version will automatically be symmetrical. You can choose a symmetrical axis at the bottom, which starts from the corresponding axis. If you select the linear section, you can adjust the pattern on the roof. ## New Layer Tool In the new version, we added the layer tool. There are these two tools in the 3D and 2D windows. First, you can choose to create a layer tool and create a layer grid. The mouse and mouse wheel version displays as a white version, while the other version appears half-transparent. You can create a layer in the 3D or 2D window. After creating a layer, you can press the Shift and Ctrl keys to divide the grid. If you need to divide the grid as a whole, you can choose the Edit Layer tool. In the menu bar in the right-hand corner, select All Dividing. Press Ctrl and Shift while holding down the left mouse button to extend the layer as needed. After selecting two points, you can merge these two points. If you need to merge two topos, you can select the topo tool and then select all merge in the output menu. In the upper right corner of the 3D window, you can see the merge window where we can set a length. If the distance between the two topos is less than the specified value, they will be merged. If there are too many merge points, you can adjust them according to your needs. ## Topo Creation and Grid Management In the process of creating a topo, you need to pay attention to any overlaps. Place the mouse on the topo that you want to create; therefore, the 2D window will be more convenient for merging topos. You can directly select the topo on the pocket topo, then refer to the output menu to create a topo on the inner layer. After creating a topo, you can select reset grid. There are two types of reset grid: colon and replacement. When you select the replacement option, it will replace the original version. If you choose Reboot, the new version will replace the original version. ## Grid Separation Tool In the new version, we added a clothing display style that can display the surface of the clothing line frame. We can see that the grid formed from the original version is consistent with when we took it out. Next, I would like to introduce our new function, grid separation. We can see that the grid of the rectangular version is relatively large. The grid refers to the distance between the top and bottom of the grid. In the new version, we have added the tool to select the grid using a brush. After selecting, the 3D window in the upper right corner can set the size of the brush. After selecting a region, we can separate it. The grid in this region will be significantly larger, while the grid in other areas may be smaller. We can change the name of the separation and the level of separation in the attribute editor in the upper right corner. The higher the level of separation, the more the grid will be smaller. If the level of separation is set to 0, the separation effect will not exist, or you can directly select the separation area and delete the separation. ## Conclusion This is a brief introduction to the grid separation function. Now we have a template. After opening the simulation, we will find that the simulation speed is very fast, but the folds are not delicate enough. After reducing the particle diameter, the number of grids will increase, and the operation speed will decrease, but the folds will be more delicate. We can see that the grid has been separated. When we need some details, we can utilize grid separation. First, use the brush tool to select the grid to be separated. After selecting the grid, we can perform the separation and start the simulation. We can observe that the details of the folds will be retained while the overall fold shape remains similar. We can select whether to display grid separation in the 3D window. Additionally, there are two optimization options. The first is the environment setting in the 3D window, where we can adjust it directly. We can choose to display the light controller, allowing us to set the light intensity and angle in Marvelous Designer. Then, the wind controller can be activated to simulate the wind effect. We can also select whether to display shadows and the 3D grid. Thank you for your attention to this finished video. Do not forget to like the video! ```
